akhfash:1-1.t: As for His words ﴿قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾, His word ﴿أَحدُ﴾ is a badal (substitute) for His word ﴿الله﴾, as if He said "He is One" (هُوَ أَحَدٌ). And among the Arabs are those who do not give it tanwīn, dropping it because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

akhfash:4-4.t: And His words ﴿وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ﴾: ﴿أَحَدٌ﴾ is the noun (ism of kāna) and ﴿كُفُوا﴾ is the khabar (predicate).

celaleyn:1-1.t: He ﷺ was asked about his Lord, so there was revealed: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾. «الله» is the khabar (predicate) of «هو», and «أحد» is a badal (substitute) from it or a second khabar.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ﴾: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), that is, the One turned to in needs, always.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿لَمْ يَلِدْ﴾, because of the absence of anything of His kind, ﴿وَلَمْ يُولَدْ﴾, because of the absence of origination in time from Him,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ﴾, that is, an equal and a like. «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كفوا» and was fronted before it because it is the focus of the intent of the negation; and «أحد», which is the ism (noun) of «يكن», was placed after its khabar (predicate) in observance of the verse-ending (fāṣila).

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿هُوَ﴾ the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of هو, and the clause «هو..» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿لَمْ يَلِدْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلَمْ يُولَدْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive imperfect verb in the jussive by lam, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿وَلَمْ يَكُنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam. ﴿لَهُ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) كفوا. ﴿كُفُواً﴾ the fronted khabar (predicate) of يكن. ﴿أَحَدٌ﴾ its postponed noun. The clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it.

farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾.
They asked the Prophet ﷺ: What is your Lord? Does He eat or drink? Is He of gold or of silver? So Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, revealed: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ﴾. Then they said: What then is He? He said: ﴿أَحَدٌ﴾. This is among His attributes: that He is One (واحد). And «أحد», even though it is indefinite — Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: he means in its wording — is nominative by being made a fresh start (istiʾnāf), like His word: ﴿هَذَا بَعْلِى شَيْخٌ﴾. Al-Kisāʾī said something that I do not consider anything: he said: «هو» is an ʿimād (support pronoun), like His word: ﴿إِنَّهُ أَنَا اللهُ﴾. So he made «أحد» nominative by «الله», and made «هو» take the place of the hāʾ in (أنه). But an ʿimād is not begun with unless there is before it inna or one of its sisters, or kāna, or [verbs of] supposing.

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كُفُواً أَحَدٌ﴾.
It is read heavy and light [i.e. «كُفُوًا» and «كُفْوًا»]. When the predicate (lit. "act") of the indefinite comes after it, it follows it [in case] with kāna and its sisters; so you say: لم يكن لعبدالله أحد نظير (ʿAbd Allāh has no one as an equal), [with «نظير» nominative]. When you put «النظير» first, they put it in the accusative and did not disagree on it, saying: لم يكن لعبدالله نظير أحد [Translator's note: printed without the accusative alif; the intended form is «نظيرًا»]. That is because when it comes after it, it follows the noun in its nominative; and when it comes first, there being nothing before it for it to follow, it reverts to the verb kāna and is made accusative.
The one who read "أحدُ اللهُ الصمدُ", dropping the nūn from (أحد), says: the nūn is the nūn of i'rab [i.e. the tanwīn]; when the alif and lām meet it, it is dropped. Likewise when a sākin (unvowelled letter) meets it, it is sometimes dropped, though that is not the [preferred] way. The readers have read: ﴿وقالت اليهود عُزَيْرُ ابنُ اللهِ﴾, and "عزيرٌ ابن الله".
Tanwīn is better. One of them recited to me:
لَتَجِدَنِّى بالأميرِ بَرّا * وبالقناةِ مِدْعَسًا مِكَرَّا * إذا غُطَيْفُ السُّلَمِىُّ فَرَّا *
(You will surely find me dutiful to the emir, and with the spear a hard thruster, charging again and again, when Ghuṭayf al-Sulamī runs away.)
And another recited to me:
كيْفَ نَومى على الفراشِ ولمّا * تَشْملِ الشَّامَ غارةٌ شعواءُ
تُذْهِلُ الشَّيخَ عن بَنيهِ وتُبدى * عن خِدامِ العقيلةُ العذراءُ
(How can I sleep on my bed when a far-flung raid has not yet engulfed Syria — one that makes the old man forget his sons, and makes the noble virgin uncover [her leg] from the anklet?)
He meant: عن خدامٍ, [with] العقيلةُ العذراءُ [as the subject]; and their saying [it is] عن خدامٍ [عقيلة] عذراء is nothing.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «هو»: the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), mubtadaʾ (subject); «الله»: a second mubtadaʾ; «أحد»: khabar (predicate) of the second; and the clause is the khabar of «هو».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «الله الصمد»: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the clause is a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ {هُوَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «لم يلد» is a third khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «أحد»: the noun of «يكن»; the preposition «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) «كفوًا».

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He (قل هو الله أحد): (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); it is the pronoun of the matter (al-ḥadīth), the report or the affair. (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (أحد) its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of (هو). Its implied form is: Say, O Muhammad, the true matter is: Allah is One. Abū ʿAmr read it with the tanwīn of (أحد) elided because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t:
His saying (الله الصمد): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). And it was said: (الصمد) is its naʿt (adjective) and what follows it is the khabar. And it was said: (الصمد) is nominative (marfūʿ) on the implication of a mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of (الله), exalted be His mention. And it was said: it is a clause that is a khabar after a khabar of (هو). And it was said: it is a badal (substitute) for (أحد); and it was said: it is a badal for the first name (الله).
This repetition occurs in the attributes only for glorification and magnification; and for that reason the name was made overt after having already appeared overtly, whereas its due was that the second be a pronoun, since it had already been mentioned overtly. But making it overt is more emphatic in glorification and magnification. Likewise He said (أصحاب الميمنة ما أصحاب الميمنة), (وأصحاب المشأمة ما أصحاب المشأمة), (الحاقة ما الحاقة) and (القارعة ما القارعة): in all of it the noun was repeated overtly after having already appeared overtly, and that is for glorification and magnification and for the sense of wonder in it. Likewise His saying (واستغفروا الله إن الله غفور): the due of all of it was to be repeated as a pronoun, but it was made overt for what we have mentioned.
(هو) occurred as a pronoun (kināya) at the beginning of the speech only because it is speech that ran as an answer to a questioner: the Jews asked the Prophet, peace be upon him, to describe his Lord to them and give His lineage, so Allah revealed: Say, O Muhammad, (هو الله أحد), i.e. the matter you asked about is: Allah is One, Allah the Eternal Refuge, to its end.
Al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said: (هو) is a pronoun for something singular [Translator's note: the printed text has «هوكناية عن مفردو الله», read as «هو كناية عن مفرد والله»], (الله) is its khabar, and (أحد) is a badal for (الله).
The origin of (أحد) is «وحد»; a hamza was substituted for the wāw, which is rare with a wāw bearing fatḥa. (أحد) has the meaning of «واحد». Ibn al-Anbārī said: (أحد) means «واحد»; the alif dropped from it according to the dialect of those who say «وحد» for «واحد», and the hamza was substituted for the wāw with fatḥa, as it was substituted in their saying «امرأة أناة» (a deliberate woman), whose origin is «وناة», from «ونى يني» when one slackens. The substitution of the hamza for a wāw with fatḥa has not been heard except in (أحد) and «أناة». And it was said: the origin of (أحد) is «واحد»; they substituted a hamza for the wāw, so two hamzas met, and one was elided for lightness; so it is «واحد» in origin. And it has been said that (أحدا) means «أول» (first), with no substitution or change in it, on a par with «اليوم الأحد» (the first day, Sunday), and like their saying «لا أحد في الدار» (there is no one in the house).
(أحد) carries a benefit not found in «واحد»: if you say «لا يقوم لزيد واحد» (not one stands up to Zayd), it is possible that two or more stand up to him; but if you say «لا يقوم له أحد» (no one stands up to him), you have negated all. This is so only in negation specifically; in affirmation it does not carry that meaning. When (أحد) has the meaning of «واحد», it occurs in affirmation: you say «مر بنا أحد», i.e. one [person] passed by us. So likewise (قل هو الله أحد), i.e. One.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying (لم يلد): its origin is «لم يولد»; the wāw was elided as it is elided from «يزن» and «يعد». Its mention has already passed repeatedly. [Translator's note: the source says «لم يولد», presumably meaning «لم يَوْلِد» (the active form with the radical wāw), not the passive (لم يولد) of the following verse.]

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying (ولم يكن له كفوا أحد): (أحد) is the noun (ism) of kāna and (كفوا) is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, with (له) being non-operative (mulghā). And it was said: (له) is the khabar, and that is the analogy of Sībawayh's view, because according to him it is ugly to make the adverbial phrase non-operative when it comes first. Al-Mubarrad disagreed with him and allowed it without ugliness, citing the verse as evidence. But there is no evidence for al-Mubarrad in the verse, because (كفوا) may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (أحد), placed before it, since the naʿt (adjective) of an indefinite noun, when it precedes it, is made accusative as a ḥāl, as they said «وقع أمر فجأة» (a matter occurred suddenly).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿قل﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت", referring to the Prophet ﷺ. The clause ﴿قل﴾ is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.
﴿هو﴾: an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿الله﴾: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, or a second mubtadaʾ, nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿أحد﴾: naʿt (adjective) of الله, or the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ, in which case the clause ﴿الله أحد﴾ is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ. The clause ﴿هو الله﴾ is in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿الله﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿الصمد﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative. The clause ﴿الله الصمد﴾ is in the position of the nominative as a second khabar of the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) هو.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿لم﴾: a particle of negation, of conversion [to the past] and of the jussive, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿يلد﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو", referring to Allah the Exalted. The clause is in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as a third khabar (predicate) of the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) هو.
﴿ولم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لم is a particle of negation, of conversion and of the jussive, indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿يولد﴾: an imperfect verb, passive, jussive by لم, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn; its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, its implied form being "هو", referring to Allah the Exalted. The clause is in the position of the nominative by conjunction to the clause لم يلد.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿ولم﴾: the wāw: a conjunction; لم: a particle of negation, of conversion [to the past] and of the jussive, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿يكن﴾: an incomplete imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn.
﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كفوا﴾.
﴿كفوا﴾: the fronted khabar (predicate) of يكن, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿أحد﴾: the delayed noun of يكن, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma. The clause is in the position of the nominative by conjunction to the clause ﴿لم يلد﴾.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: The wāw is retained in the second [verb, «يولد»] and dropped in the first [«يلد»], because in the first it fell between a yāʾ and a kasra, while in the second it fell between a yāʾ and a fatḥa. «[Translator's note: the two verbs referred to are «لم يلد» and «ولم يولد», from the root و ل د.]»

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
Ḥamza's reading is «كفوا». Hārūn the Reader claimed that Sulaymān ibn ʿAlī al-Hāshimī read «ولم يكن له كفئا أحد», and the meaning is the same, as [the poet] said: [al-Basīṭ] 597-
لا تقذفنّي بركن لا كفاء له ... وإن تأثّفك الأعداء بالرّفد
(Do not hurl at me a mighty pillar that has no equal (كفاء), even if the enemies surround you with their reinforcements.)
Likewise كفيّ, whose plural is أكفية. If you say كفوء and كفء, their plural is أكفاء. One says: "So-and-so withholds his daughters except from the أكفاء (equals)." So it is possible that كفو and كفء are two dialectal forms with one meaning, and it is possible that كفء is a lightened form of كفؤ, just as one says رسل and كتب [for رسُل and كتُب]. «كفوا» is the khabar (predicate) of يكن, and «أحد» is the ism (subject) of يكن. This is the view of most grammarians. However, Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] held Sībawayh to be in error in his preference for making the ẓarf (adverbial / prepositional phrase) the khabar when it is placed first — for he [Sībawayh] prefers: إنّ في الدار زيدا جالسا — and he faulted him by means of this verse, because if «له» were the khabar, «كفوا» would not be put in the accusative as the khabar of يكن. Yet Sībawayh did in fact allow the ẓarf to be placed first without being the khabar, and he cited: [al-Rajaz] 598- ما دام فيهنّ فصيل حيّا (as long as a weaned young camel among them is alive) — and the poem rhymes in the accusative. There is another view on the accusative of كفو which I do not know any of the grammarians to have mentioned, namely that it is accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an indefinite noun placed before it, and so it is put in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), just as you say:
جاءني مسرعا رجل (a man came to me hurrying), and as [the poet] said: [Majzūʾ al-Wāfir] 599- لميّة موحشا طلل (Mayya has a desolate ruin). But al-Farrāʾ mentioned that one says: ما كان ثمّ أحد نظير لزيد (there was no one there equal to Zayd), and if you place it first you say: ما كان ثمّ نظيرا لزيد أحد; and he did not mention the reason that necessitated this.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: هُوَ is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), a pronoun standing for "the matter" (ḍamīr al-ḥadīth / al-shaʾn), on the view of most of the Basrans and al-Kisāʾī, i.e., "the matter, which is the truth: Allah is One".

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
There are six construals of it. The best is that your saying اللَّهُ is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), الصَّمَدُ its naʿt (adjective), and what follows it its khabar (predicate). The second view is that الصمد is the khabar. The third is that it is on the implication of a mubtadaʾ. The fourth, that it is a khabar after a khabar. The fifth, that it is a badal (substitute) for أحد. The sixth, that it is a badal for your first saying الله.
If it is asked: what is the meaning of the repetition (of الله)? The answer is that it carries magnification; such is the speech of the Arabs, as the poet said: [al-Khafīf] 592-
لا أرى الموت يسبق الموت شيء ... نغّص الموت ذا الغنى والفقيرا
(I see nothing that outstrips death; death has troubled the rich and the poor alike.)
He magnified the matter of death by repeating it and not using a pronoun for it; and similar is وَاسْتَغْفِرُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ [al-Muzzammil: 20].
Al-Farrāʾ does not permit (هو) to be a pronoun for "the matter" unless something precedes it. This is an arbitrary imposition on the language; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: يا مُوسى إِنَّهُ أَنَا اللَّهُ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ [al-Naml: 9], and إنّ (here) is at the beginning [Translator's note: the text reads «وإنّي الابتداء», apparently for «وإنّ في الابتداء»], and إنّ only enters upon a mubtadaʾ by consensus. Also, «هو», if it is not a pronoun for "the matter", is a mubtadaʾ at the beginning of the sūra. If someone asks: then to what does it refer? His proof is the ḥadīth that the Jews asked the Prophet ﷺ to describe his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to them and give His lineage, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: I have dictated this ḥadīth so that it may be known as I heard it; there are things in it. Among them: it is from the ḥadīth of Jarīr [Translator's note: so in the text; evidently Juwaybir, as named next] from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who did not hear from Ibn ʿAbbās. Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb said: Juwaybir ibn Saʿīd, a Khurāsānī who narrates from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, is abandoned in ḥadīth (matrūk al-ḥadīth). And in it is Ismāʿīl ibn Ziyād, who is weak. We have mentioned it with what is in it so that it may be known. And in it is "al-Baʿlabakkī", as the Shaykh said, while the better form is "al-Baʿlī"; and this is permissible according to the Kufans, and we have explained it at His saying, Mighty and Majestic: عَلَيْها تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ [al-Muddaththir: 30] [Translator's note: this sentence appears out of place in the text].
And al-Akhfash Saʿīd: his view is like the view of al-Farrāʾ, in that it (هو) is a pronoun for a singular (noun); «الله» is the khabar. Al-Akhfash said: «أحد» is a badal for «الله». Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Isḥāq read أَحَدٌ اللَّهُ without nunation [Translator's note: the printed vowelling shows nunation; the reading described is أَحَدُ اللَّهُ], and likewise it is narrated from Abān ibn ʿUthmān; they dropped the nunation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Sībawayh recited: [al-Mutaqārib] 593- ولا ذاكر الله إلّا قليلا ("nor remembering Allah except a little"); and al-Farrāʾ recited: [al-Khafīf] 594-
كيف نومي على الفراش ولمّا ... تشمل الشّام غارة شعواء
تذهل الشّيخ عن بنيه وتلوي ... عن خدام العقلة العذراء
(How can I sleep on my bed when a widespread raid has not yet engulfed Syria — one that makes the old man forget his sons and lays bare the anklets of the secluded virgin?)
He means عن خدامٍ العقيلة, dropping the nunation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, just as they read أَحَدٌ اللَّهُ. The better course is to give the nunation a vowel because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, since it is a (grammatical) mark and dropping it is ugly; and the reading of the community is more fitting.
Concerning «أحد» there are three views. Among them: أحد is in the sense of waḥad, and waḥad is in the sense of wāḥid, as the poet said: [al-Basīṭ] 595-
كأنّ رحلي وقد زال النّهار بنا ... يوم الجليل على مستأنس وحد
(As if my saddle, when the day had declined with us on the day of al-Jalīl, were upon a lone, wary wild bull.)
So the wāw was replaced by a hamza. The second view is that the original is wāḥid; the wāw was replaced by a hamza, and the (other) hamza was dropped so that two hamzas would not meet. The third view is that aḥad is in the sense of awwal (first), as you say "the day al-aḥad" — and "the day al-awwal" is heard from the Arabs.
Some of the people of reasoning said: in أحد there is a benefit that is not in واحد, because if you say "so-and-so has no one (wāḥid) who stands up to him" [Translator's note: the text reads «يا قوم» here and below, evidently for «يقوم»], it is possible that two or more stand up to him; but if you say "so-and-so has no one (aḥad) who stands up to him", it includes the meaning of one and more. Abū Jaʿfar said:
This is a mistake; there is no disagreement among the grammarians that أحد, when it is like this, only occurs in negation, as the poet said:
[al-Basīṭ] 596-
وقفت فيها أصيلا كي أسائلها ... عيّت جوابا وما بالرّبع من أحد
(I stood there in the late afternoon to question it; it was unable to answer, and there was no one in the encampment.)
But when it is in the sense of wāḥid, it occurs in affirmation. You say: "no one (aḥad) passed by us", i.e., no single one; and likewise قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {قُلْ هُوَ الله أَحَدٌ}: concerning «هو» there are two views. The first: it is a pronoun referring back to what is understood from the context, for it is related in the occasions of revelation that they said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Describe your Lord to us and give His lineage." It was also said: they said to him: "Is He of copper or of iron?" — so it was revealed. On this view «الله» may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «أَحَدٌ» its khabar (predicate), the clause being the khabar of the first [«هو»]. «اللَّهُ» may also be a badal (substitute) with «أحدٌ» the khabar; or «اللَّهُ» a first khabar and «أحدٌ» a second khabar; or «أحدٌ» the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He is One". The second: it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), because it is a place of magnification, and the clause after it is its explanatory khabar.
The hamza of «أحد» is substituted for a wāw, because it is from al-waḥda (oneness); and the substitution of hamza for a wāw with fatḥa [Translator's note: the sentence is left incomplete in the source; the sense is that such a substitution is rare]. It was said: from it is "imraʾa anāh" (a deliberate, slow woman), from al-wanā, which is languor. The difference was given before between this «أحد» and the «أحد» meant for generality, for the hamza of that one is itself original. Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted that the hamza of this «أحد» is not changed, but is itself original, like the one meant for generality; but the well-known view is the first. Thaʿlab distinguished between «واحد» and «أحد»: wāḥid admits counting, the plural and the dual, whereas aḥad does not admit that; one says "Allah is aḥad" but one does not say "Zayd is aḥad", because Allah the Exalted has this exclusive quality, whereas Zayd has various states. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected this from him: "One says aḥad wa-ʿishrūn (twenty-one) and the like, so counting does enter it." — end of quote. Makkī said: "aḥad was originally waḥad; the wāw was changed into hamza, so two alifs came together, because the hamza resembles the alif; so one of them was dropped for lightness." [Translator's note: so in the source.]
ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] and Ubayy read {اللَّهُ أحدٌ} without «قُلْ». The Prophet ﷺ read «أحدٌ» without «قل هو». Al-Aʿmash read: «قل هو اللَّهُ الواحد».
The generality read «أحدٌ» with tanwīn, which is the original. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Abān ibn ʿUthmān, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, al-Ḥasan, Abū al-Sammāl, and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission, among a great number, read it with the tanwīn dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, as in his saying:
4675 - عمرُو الذي هَشَمَ الثَّريدَ لقومِه ... ورجالُ مكةَ مُسْنِتُون عِجافُ
(ʿAmr, who crumbled bread into broth for his people when the men of Mecca were famine-struck and emaciated.)
Another said:
4676 - فأَلْفَيْتُه غيرَ مُسْتَعْتِبٍ ... ولا ذاكرَ اللَّهَ إلاَّ قليلا
(I found him not seeking to make amends, nor remembering Allah except a little.)

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {الصمد}: on the pattern faʿal in the sense of mafʿūl, like al-qabaḍ and al-naqaḍ. He is the master to whom one turns (yuṣmadu ilayhi) in needs, i.e. who is sought, and none is able to fulfil them except Him. The following was recited:
4677 - ألا بَكَّرَ النَّاعي بخَيْرِ بني أسدْ ... بعَمْرِو بن مسعودٍ وبالسَّيِّد الصَّمَدْ
(Lo, the announcer of death came early with [news of] the best of Banū Asad — ʿAmr ibn Masʿūd, the master to whom all turned.)
Another said:
4678 - عَلَوْتُه بحُسامٍ ثم قُلْتُ له ... خُذْها حُذَيْفُ فأنتَ السَّيِّدُ الصَّمَدُ
(I came down on him with a sharp sword, then said to him: "Take it, Ḥudhayf, for you are the master to whom all turn.")
It was also said: al-ṣamad is that which has no hollow; from it is his saying:
4679 - شِهابُ حُروبٍ لا تَزال جيادُه ... عوابِسَ يَعْلُكْنَ الشَّكِيْمَ المُصَمَّدا
(A blazing star of wars, whose steeds are ever grim-faced, champing on the solid bit.)
Ibn Kaʿb said: its explanation is what follows it, namely His saying «لم يَلِدْ ولم يُوْلَدُ»; this resembles what they said in explaining al-halūʿ. The best [view] of this clause is that it is independent, with the benefit of this predication. «الصَّمَدُ» may also be an adjective, with the khabar (predicate) being in the clause after it; so it was said, but it is weak from the standpoint of the context, for the context requires each clause to be independent in its predication.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {كُفُواً أَحَدٌ}: concerning its accusative there are two views. The first: it is the khabar (predicate) of «يكنْ», «أحدٌ» is its noun (ism), and «له» is attached to the khabar, i.e. "and none is equal to Him". Al-Mubarrad objected to Sībawayh with this verse, inasmuch as he [Sībawayh] claims that when the adverbial phrase (ẓarf) is placed first it is the khabar, whereas here He did not make it the khabar despite its being placed first.
Al-Mubarrad was answered in two ways. The first: Sībawayh did not make that obligatory, but only permitted it. The second: we do not concede that the adverbial phrase here is not a khabar; rather it is the khabar, and «كُفُواً» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), as will be explained. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Eloquent Arabic speech is to postpone the adverbial phrase that is laghw (dependent, not standing as a predicate) and not mustaqarr, and not to place it first; Sībawayh stated this explicitly in his Kitāb. So why is it placed first in the most eloquent and purest speech? I say: this discourse was brought only to negate equivalence from the essence of the Creator, exalted is He, and the focus and centre of this meaning is this adverbial phrase; so for that reason it was the most important, the most relevant, and the most deserving and worthy of being placed first."
The second: it is accusative as a ḥāl from «أحد», because it was its adjective, and when it was placed before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl, and «له» is the khabar; Makkī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and others said this. It may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun latent (mustakinn) in the prepositional phrase, since it occurs as khabar. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān], after relating the words of al-Zamakhsharī and Makkī, said: "This clause is not of this category, because in His saying {وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ} the preposition and its genitive noun are not complete (tāmm); it is only incomplete (nāqiṣ), not fit to be the khabar of «كان»; rather it is attached to «كُفُواً» and placed before it. The implied form is: 'and none is equivalent to Him'. So it is in the sense of the object, attached to «كُفُواً», and was placed before «كُفُواً» because of concern for it, since it contains the pronoun of the Creator, exalted is He. And the khabar was placed in the middle, even though its origin is to be postponed, because the postponed noun is a verse-ending (fāṣila), so that was fitting.
On the basis of what we have established, the parsing of Makkī and others — that «له» is the khabar and «كُفُواً» a ḥāl from «أحد» — is void, because it is an incomplete adverbial phrase not fit to be a khabar. By that al-Zamakhsharī's question and answer are also void. Sībawayh spoke only of the adverbial phrase that is fit to be a khabar or not to be. Sībawayh said: 'You say: «ما كان فيها أحدٌ خيرٌ منك», «وما كان [أحدٌ] مثلُك فيها», and «ليس أحدٌ فيها خيرٌ منك», when you make «فيها» mustaqarr (predicative) and do not construe it as in your saying «فيها زيدٌ قائمٌ»: you make the adjective follow the noun. If you construe it as «فيها زيدٌ قائمٌ», you use the accusative and say: «ما كان فيها أحدٌ خيراً منك» and «وما كان أحدٌ خيراً منك فيها». Except that when you intend cancellation (ilghāʾ), the further you postpone what is cancelled the better; and when you intend it to be mustaqarr, the further forward you place it the better. Placing first, postponing, cancellation and predication are all good, frequent Arabic. The Exalted said: {وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ}, and the poet said:
4680 - ما دامَ فيهِنَّ فَصِيْلٌ حَيَّاً ...
(As long as there is among them a weaned young camel alive…)'
— end of Sībawayh's words." The Shaykh said: "You see his words and his illustration with the adverbial phrase that is fit to be a khabar. The meaning of his saying 'mustaqarr' is: a khabar of the mubtadaʾ or of kāna. If you say: but he gave the verse as an example — I say: this is what led Makkī, al-Zamakhsharī and others into what they fell into. Sībawayh only meant that the complete adverbial phrase, which is in his saying:
ما دامَ فيهِنَّ فَصِيلٌ حَيَّاً ...
is treated as an extra element (faḍla), not as a khabar, just as «له» in the verse is treated as an extra element; so he made the adverbial phrase that could be a khabar like the incomplete adverbial phrase in not being used as a khabar. No one with a sound mind doubts that no statement is formed from «له أحد»; indeed, if «كُفُو» were postponed and made nominative as an adjective while «له» was made the khabar, no statement would be formed from it. Rather you see that the negation applies only to the khabar, which is «كُفُواً», and the meaning is: none is equivalent to Him." — end of what the Shaykh said.
His saying "no one doubts…" to its end is an attempt to overawe the reader. Otherwise his saying "this adverbial phrase is incomplete" is not conceded, because the incomplete adverbial phrase refers to one in whose predication there is no benefit, like one cut off from annexation, and like «في دارٍ رجلٌ». He transmitted from Sībawayh the preceding examples, such as «ما كان فيها أحدٌ خيراً منك» — and what is the difference between this and the noble verse? And how can he say this when Sībawayh said at the end of his words: "Placing first, postponing, cancellation and predication are all good, frequent Arabic"?
The generality read with ḍamma on the kāf and the fāʾ [«كُفُؤاً»]. Al-Aʿraj, Shayba and Nāfiʿ in one transmission eased (sahhala) the hamza. Ḥamza made the fāʾ quiescent [«كُفْؤاً»] and changed the hamza into wāw in pause only. Ḥafṣ changed it into wāw in all cases. The rest read with hamza in all cases. Discussion of this was given at the beginning of al-Baqara at His saying: {هُزُواً} [al-Baqara: 67].
Sulaymān ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās read «كِفاءٌ» with kasra and lengthening, i.e. He has no like. The following by al-Nābigha was recited:
4681 - لا تَقْذِفَنِّي برُكْنٍ لا كِفاءَ له ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Do not hurl at me a force [lit. a pillar] that has no equal…)
Nāfiʿ, in one transmission, read «كِفا» with kasra and fatḥa on the fāʾ, without lengthening, as though he transferred the vowel of the hamza and dropped it. Al-kufʾ: the counterpart; "this is a kufʾ for you", i.e. your counterpart; the noun is al-kafāʾa, with fatḥa.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ اللَّهُ (١)).
The words of the Exalted (هُوَ): there are two views on it. The first: it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and «اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the khabar of «هُوَ».
The second: it is a mubtadaʾ in the sense of "the one asked about", because they said: "Is your Lord of copper or of gold?" On this view «اللَّهُ» may be the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and «أَحَدٌ» a badal (substitute), or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. It is also possible for «اللَّهُ» to be a badal and «أَحَدٌ» the khabar. The hamza of «أَحَد» is substituted for a wāw, because it is in the sense of «الْوَاحِد» (the One); the substitution of hamza for a wāw bearing fatḥa is rare, and an instance of it is «امْرَأَةٌ أَنَاةٌ» (a deliberate, unhurried woman), i.e. «وَنَاةٌ», because it is from «الْوَنَى» (slackness).
It is also said that the hamza is original, like the hamza in «أَحَد» used for generality. Whoever drops the tanwīn (nunation) from «أَحَد» does so because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. [Translator's note: the verse is quoted in the source with «اللَّهُ» from the following verse (اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ) attached to it.]

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ (٤)).
The words of the Exalted (كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ): [«أَحَدٌ»] is the noun (ism) of «كَانَ». There are two views on its khabar (predicate):
The first: «كُفُوًا»; on this view «لَهُ» may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «كُفُوًا», because the implied form is «وَلَمْ يَكُنْ أَحَدٌ كُفُوًا لَهُ» (and none is equal to Him), or it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَكُنْ».
The second view: that the khabar is «لَهُ», and «كُفُوًا» is a ḥāl from «أَحَدٌ», i.e. «وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ أَحَدٌ كُفُوًا»; when the indefinite [adjective] was fronted, it was put in the accusative as a ḥāl. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ هو اللَّهُ أحَدٌ﴾ ﴿اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ﴾ [al-Ikhlāṣ: 2] ("Say: He is Allah, One; Allah, the Eternal Refuge"), with tanwīn on ”أحَدٌ“. It was read without the tanwīn: ”أحَدُ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ“; and it was read with the dāl made vowelless and the tanwīn omitted. As for omitting the tanwīn, it is likewise because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, except that it is the vowellessness of two vowelless letters [Translator's note: so in the source, «سُكُون السّاكِنَيْنِ»; the text appears corrupt here]. Whoever makes it vowelless intends a pause, then begins anew and says: ﴿اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ﴾ [al-Ikhlāṣ: 2].
As for ”هو“: ”هُوَ“ is an allusion (kināya, pronoun) referring to the mention of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; the meaning is: "The One Whose lineage you asked to have made clear is Allah." And ”أحَدٌ“ is nominative on the sense ”هُوَ أحَدٌ هو اللَّهُ“ ("He is One; He is Allah"), so ”هُوَ“ is mubtadaʾ (subject). And ”هُوَ“ may be [the pronoun] of the matter (ḍamīr al-amr), as you say ”هُوَ زَيْدٌ قائِمٌ“, that is, "the matter is: Zayd is standing"; and the meaning is: "the matter is: Allah is One".

zajjaj:2-2.t:
And His saying: ﴿اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ﴾: it is related in the exegesis «that the polytheists said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Give us the lineage of your Lord", so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down: ﴿قُلْ هو اللَّهُ أحَدٌ﴾ [al-Ikhlāṣ: 1]». The explanation of ﴿الصَّمَدُ﴾ is: the lord in whom lordship culminates. The poet said:
لَقَدْ بَكَّرَ النّاعِي بِخَيْرَيْ بَنِي أسَدْ ∗∗∗ بِعَمْرِو بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ وبِالسَّيِّدِ الصَّمَدْ
(The announcer of death came early with [news of] the two best of Banū Asad: ʿAmr ibn Masʿūd and the lord, the ṣamad.)
And it was said: ”اَلصَّمَدُ“ is the one who has no hollow. And it was said: ”اَلصَّمَدُ“ is the one to whom everything turns (ṣamada lahu) [in need], and Who created all things, without Whom nothing can do; and all of them point to His oneness. All of these attributes may be applied to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أحَدٌ﴾ ("and there is none equal to Him"): there are four ways of reading in it: ﴿كُفُوًا﴾ with ḍamma on the kāf and the fāʾ; ”كُفْوًا“ with ḍamma on the kāf and sukūn on the fāʾ; ”كِفْوًا“ with kasra on the kāf and sukūn on the fāʾ, and it has been read so; and ”كِفاءً“ with kasra on the kāf. And ”اَلْكُفْءُ“, with fatḥa on the kāf [Translator's note: so in the source; the form printed has ḍamma] and sukūn on the fāʾ, is a noun; it was not read so. There is another way in it which is not permissible in reading. One says: ”فُلانٌ كُفْءُ فُلانٍ“ ("so-and-so is the equal of so-and-so"), like ”كُفِيُّ فُلانٍ“.
It has come in the ḥadīth «that ﴿قُلْ هو اللَّهُ أحَدٌ﴾ [al-Ikhlāṣ: 1] is equal to a third of the Qur'an, ﴿قُلْ يا أيُّها الكافِرُونَ﴾ [al-Kāfirūn: 1] is equal to a quarter of the Qur'an, and ﴿إذا زُلْزِلَتِ﴾ [al-Zalzala: 1] is equal to half of the Qur'an».
